Does the digestion protocol affect the chemical integrity of the synthetic polymers?

Hit Quality Index (HQI) values ranged from 89.71% to 99.31%. PE (90 µm) and PET (250 µm) demonstrated excellent spectral agreement (HQI ≥ 95%), while PP (90 µm), PA-66 (100 µm), and PE (35 µm) showed good agreement (HQI: 91.72% – 93.05%). PMMA (250 µm) had slightly lower values (89.71% HQI), however pre- and post-degradation spectra showed good similarity. Furthermore, staining the MP particles with NRD did not appear to interfere with ATR-FTIR identification under the conditions used in this study.

What does an actual sample of Mytilus galloprovincialis look like?

Drag the handle to compare Fig. 11a and Fig. 11b.

What does an actual sediment sample from the seafloor look like after microplastics have been extracted by density separation using K₂CO₃ (1.56 g cm⁻³)?

Drag the handle to compare Fig. 12a and Fig. 12b.

Shells with cavities contain air, which makes it very difficult to extract microplastics completely (without sediment residues) based on density. Some microplastics are difficult to see with the naked eye without Nile red staining.
